title: TBNet: A Neural Architectural Defense Framework Facilitating DNN Model Protection in Trusted Execution Environments
problem: Existing TEE-based solutions for protecting DNN models on edge devices either provide inadequate protection or introduce large performance overhead. There is a critical need to balance security and performance when protecting DNN models from extraction on resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Protecting DNN models on edge devices from extraction and theft is increasingly important as edge computing expands, requiring solutions that minimize performance overhead.
method: TBNet uses a Two-Branch approach that splits neural network execution between two places: a regular processor (the untrusted REE—Rich Execution Environment) and a physically-isolated secure zone (the TEE—Trusted Execution Environment). Non-sensitive layers run on the regular processor to maintain speed, while sensitive layers run in the secure zone to prevent the model from being copied or stolen. The system analyzes the neural network structure to automatically determine which layers are sensitive and where to split them.
key_novelty: TBNet's Two-Branch approach partitions neural network layers between a regular processor and a secure protected zone to simultaneously protect the model from theft and maintain system performance.
contributions: TBNet framework enabling efficient DNN model protection through neural architectural partitioning between TEE and REE
Two-Branch substitution model architecture for optimized TEE/REE computation distribution
Demonstration of low-cost model protection on Raspberry Pi across diverse DNN architectures
Balanced approach providing security guarantees with minimal latency overhead

metrics.accuracy: model protection efficiency with low performance cost

limitations: Specific threat models, security assumptions, memory overhead, and scalability constraints not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Secure DNN inference on edge devices via TEE/REE partitioning
